summary: Nine comment-endorsed discoveries spanning developer tools, local speech, Android, media and interactive web experiments.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Oxc
items.source_story_title: Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust
items.summary: Rust-powered JavaScript and TypeScript tooling; a user praises its speed.
items.why_included: A first-hand endorsement of an established alternative surfaced inside compiler-rewrite discussion.
items.evidence: A user of Oxc tooling welcomes Rust rewrites and describes using the fastest tools.

evidence_sources.author: frangonf
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use oxc tooling and it's great to see the rust rewrite singularity in action and get to ride the fastest horses

items.name: OpenBSD
items.summary: Security-focused Unix operating system; a jump-host user praises its simplicity and documentation.
items.why_included: The recommendation names a practical use case and explicitly encourages hands-on exploration.
items.evidence: A year-long bastion-host user praises OpenBSD's small process list, pf and manuals, while noting it is not their daily driver.

evidence_sources.author: ctolsen
evidence_sources.excerpt: OpenBSD just feels like a *nix system is supposed to. `ps aux` is like 10 entries at first. `pf` makes so much sense. `man` pages are consistently incredible.

items.name: Nordwand Mono
items.source_story_title: Nordwand Mono – A monospace font for coders and adventurers
items.summary: Monospaced coding font; a Berkeley Mono user finds its shapes softer and nicer.
items.why_included: A concrete aesthetic comparison independently endorses the submitted font.
items.evidence: A Berkeley Mono user says Nordwand feels softer and nicer, while acknowledging subjective impressions.

evidence_sources.author: jan_m_savage
evidence_sources.excerpt: But I think Nordwand feels softer and nicer, it embodies a message in the font (thus the fluency effect is more potent).

items.name: Kokoro
items.summary: Compact local text-to-speech model; a user turns PDFs and EPUBs into audiobooks.
items.why_included: A strong first-hand sound-quality endorsement supports resurfacing after the 90-day cooldown.
items.evidence: A user calls Kokoro the best-sounding local TTS engine they have heard and uses it for PDF and EPUB audiobooks.

evidence_sources.author: gavinray
evidence_sources.excerpt: Best sounding local TTS engine I've heard by far is Kokoro It's small enough to be run on modern phones realtime, I use it for listening to PDF's/EPUB as Audiobooks

items.name: microG
items.source_story_title: MicroG: Free-libre re-implementation of Google's proprietary Android user space
items.summary: Free-software Android Google-services replacement; a LineageOS user explicitly recommends their daily setup.
items.why_included: An explicit endorsement comes from someone using the software on their main phone.
items.evidence: A main-device user says microG with LineageOS works really well and recommends it.

evidence_sources.author: hgfygkh
evidence_sources.excerpt: My main device uses MicroG with LineageOS. It works really well, and I recommend it.

items.name: ATV Launcher Pro
items.summary: Android TV home-screen replacement; users praise escaping Google's advertising-heavy default launcher.
items.why_included: Two independent first-hand endorsements identify a practical quality-of-life upgrade.
items.evidence: One user calls replacing Google's launcher with ATV Launcher Pro one of their best quality-of-life upgrades; a Shield TV user independently calls it great.

evidence_sources.author: cube00
evidence_sources.excerpt: Replacing the Google launcher (I used ATV Launcher Pro) was one of the best quality of life upgrades I've ever done, if you haven't already I highly recommend it.

items.name: Switchfin
items.summary: Native Jellyfin media client; a home-built Linux TV setup user reports easy operation.
items.why_included: A concrete media-client recommendation appears inside a working DIY television setup.
items.evidence: A commenter using Switchfin in their replacement TV interface says its Linux version works pretty well out of the box.

evidence_sources.author: darkwater
evidence_sources.excerpt: Switchfin (which has a Linux version) works pretty well out of the box

items.name: Weball
items.summary: Browser game that rolls up websites Katamari-style; fun, with reported frame-rate limits.
items.why_included: Hands-on praise supports a playful discovery, with a specific performance caveat preserved.
items.evidence: Two players praise the fun of rolling up websites; one reports poor frame rates after a few hundred words.

evidence_sources.author: OuterVale
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is such fun. I just went along and rolled up a few websites, including my own. Great little bit of web whimsy.

evidence_sources.author: gavmor
evidence_sources.excerpt: Horrible framerate after a few hundred words, but super fun until then!

items.name: River Bend Lab
items.summary: Interactive river-meander simulation; a commenter spent nearly an hour exploring its animations.
items.why_included: An enthusiastic hands-on recommendation leads beyond the submitted furniture visualization.
items.evidence: A commenter says they enjoy Ryan Sael's animations and spent a good part of an hour exploring River Bend.
